title: analysis.address.references result
description: Every reference the code makes, or every reference to one address, with the true total beside a capped list.

target.description: The address the request asked about, when it named one.

site.description: Hunk offset of the referencing instruction.

kind.description: How the operand names its target. The two absolute forms are distinct because their encodings are: an absolute-long operand may be patched by a HUNK_RELOC32 record and so can name a hunk offset, while no relocation record patches sixteen bits, so an absolute-short target is an absolute address and nothing else.

target.description: The referenced address, in the frame its addressing mode uses: an encoded absolute address (sign-extended for the short form), or a hunk offset for a PC-relative operand. The three are not interchangeable, which is why the kind travels with it.

target_address.description: The runtime address the target names, where that can be said. Absent for a PC-relative operand with no mapped origin.

reference_total.description: References matching the request before the cap. Always the true total.

relocations.description: Relocation sites whose stored pointer names the requested target, searched across the whole image rather than the analyzed hunk: a pointer to this address is a reference to it wherever it sits. Empty when the request named no target.

stored_offset.description: The offset stored at the site. Absent when the stored longword could not be read.
